chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'What is the limit of generosity?' He said, 'You give out from your wealth the right that Allah has obligated upon you, and place it in its appropriate place.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of true generosity according to the Imams?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) grounds the virtue of generosity (sakhā') in the precise fulfillment of obligatory dues (ḥaqq), such as Zakat and Khums, rather than in supererogatory excess. This definition reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on structural justice and the purification of wealth through mandatory channels before voluntary charity. It serves as a corrective to popular notions of generosity that may neglect foundational religious obligations.
